Subgroup analysis table for a meta-analysis

Source: R/meta_subgroups.R
apa_subgroups.Rd

Makes an APA-style table of a subgroup analysis of a meta-analysis fit with metafor::rma(): the pooled estimate of each subgroup, followed by the overall pooled estimate, with the test of subgroup differences in the note.

Usage

apa_subgroups(fit, subgroup, tau2 = c("separate", "common"), transform = TRUE)

Arguments

fit

a meta-analysis without moderators fit with metafor::rma()

subgroup

the subgroup variable: the name of a column in the data of fit (quoted or unquoted), or a vector with one value for each effect size. Effect sizes whose subgroup is missing are left out of the subgroups (but not of the overall estimate).

tau2

"separate" (default) for a \(\tau^2\) for each subgroup, or "common" for one \(\tau^2\) shared by all subgroups

transform

if TRUE (default), estimates computed on a transformed scale are shown on their original scale, as in apa_parameters()

Value

apa7_tbl (tibble)

Details

With tau2 = "separate" (default), each subgroup is pooled with its own random-effects model (with the estimator of \(\tau^2\) of fit), and the subgroup estimates are compared with \(Q_{\text{between}}\), the heterogeneity statistic of an equal-effects meta-analysis of the subgroup estimates. With tau2 = "common", the subgroups share one \(\tau^2\): the estimates come from a mixed-effects meta-regression with the subgroup as a categorical moderator, and the subgroups are compared with the omnibus test of the moderator (\(Q_{\text{M}}\)). The separate approach suits subgroups that may differ in heterogeneity; the common approach gives more stable estimates of \(\tau^2\) when subgroups have few studies (Borenstein et al., 2009, chap. 19).

Estimates are shown on the same scale as in apa_parameters() (e.g., risk ratios are exponentiated, and Fisher's z values are converted back to correlations).

References

Borenstein, M., Hedges, L. V., Higgins, J. P. T., & Rothstein, H. R. (2009). Introduction to meta-analysis. Wiley. doi:10.1002/9780470743386

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("metafor", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("metadat", quietly = TRUE)) {
  d_bcg <- metafor::escalc(
    measure = "RR",
    ai = tpos, bi = tneg, ci = cpos, di = cneg,
    data = metadat::dat.bcg
  )
  fit_meta <- metafor::rma(yi, vi, data = d_bcg)
  apa_subgroups(fit_meta, alloc)
}
#> # A tibble: 4 × 6
#>   Alloc      `*k*` `*RR*` `95% CI`     `*p*` `*I*^2^ (%)`
#>   <chr>      <chr> <chr>  <chr>        <chr> <chr>       
#> 1 alternate  2     0.58   [0.34, 1.01]  .06  82.0        
#> 2 random     7     0.38   [0.22, 0.65] <.001 89.9        
#> 3 systematic 4     0.65   [0.32, 1.32]  .24  86.4        
#> 4 Overall    13    0.49   [0.34, 0.70] <.001 92.2        
# }
